title: Paid Idioms - Part (ii) (SSC CGL 2018)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
True friends stay by our side through thick and thin
questions.solution: A) Through thick and thin(idiom) – in both good and bad times, under all circumstances.हर परिस्थिति में

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
Due to increased number of lay offs in the industry, the sword of Damocles is always hanging over the employees
questions.solution: C) The sword of Damocles(idiom) - a situation or threat of impending danger or harm, always felt as though it is about to happen.सिरपरलटकतीतलवार

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
The boss is going to blow his top when he discovers the blatant mistake in the balance sheet
questions.solution: C) blow his top(idiom) - Be very angryबहुत गुस्सा होना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
A mountaineer has to walk the tight rope as a small slip can prove to be fatal
questions.solution: B) Walk the tight rope(idiom) - To be in a situation in which one must be very cautious or balanced in one's actions.सतर्क रहना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
Extreme poverty made the poor woman wonder how long she could keep the wolf from the door
questions.solution: A) Keep the wolf from the door(idiom) - avoid starvation.भूख से मरने से बचना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
The ambitious project to impart free books to all students ended in smoke.
questions.solution: C) "Ended in smoke" (idiom) – yielded no result.फलहीन परिणाम

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
When his envious competitor extended a hand of friendship, he smelt a rat.
questions.solution: A) Smelt a rat(idiom) – to recognize that something is not as it appears to be or that something dishonest is happening.कुछ गलत होने की भाँप लेना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
Coming from an affluent family, she found herself a square peg in a round hole when she married a poor farmer and moved to a small village.
questions.solution: C) A square peg in a round hole(idiom) - a person who does not fit in a particular place or situation.असंगत स्थिति में होना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
It is unfortunate that most people in the country are still living from hand to mouth.
options: 1) consuming daily what little is earned
questions.solution: A) Living from hand to mouth(idiom) – barely having enough resources to survive, without saving for the future.दिन-प्रतिदिन जीविका करना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence.
The loyal watchman was cut to the quick when he was accused of theft
questions.solution: C) Cut to the quick(idiom) – deeply hurt or wounded emotionally.दिलकोआघातपहुँचाना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
butterflies in the stomach
questions.solution: B) Butterflies in the stomach(idiom) – A feeling of nervousness before an important or stressful event.उत्साहित होना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Out of the woods
questions.solution: A) out of the woods(idiom) – no longer in a difficult or dangerous situation.संकट से बाहर

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Couch potato
options: 1) a person who sleeps all day
2) a person who watches too much television
3) a person who remains relaxed and calm
4) a person who is simple in nature
questions.solution: B) Couch potato(noun) – a person who watches too much televisionटीवी देखने वाला आलस्यप्रवृत्त व्यक्ति

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Lead someone by the nose
options: 2) to force someone to take the blame
questions.solution: C) Lead someone by the nose(idiom) – to dominate someone or control someone completelyनक पकड़कर ले जाना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Give someone the cold shoulder
questions.solution: A) Give someone the cold shoulder(idiom)- ignore someoneकिसी को अनदेखा करना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Pull yourself together
questions.solution: B) Pull yourself together(idiom) – Regain one's composure or calm down.अपने आप को संभालना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Pull someone's leg
questions.solution: B) Pull someone's leg(idiom) – To tease or joke with someone, often by trying to convince them of something untrue.मजाक उड़ाना

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Actions speak louder than words
options: 1) take up a task that you cannot finish
2) what you do is more important than what you say
4) look for solutions in the wrong place
questions.solution: B) Actions speak louder than words(phrase) – what you do is more important than what you say.किसी के काम उसकी बातों से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण होते हैं।

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Costs an arm and a leg
questions.solution: D)costs an arm and a leg(idiom) – very expensiveबहुत महंगा

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Get out of hand
questions.solution: A) Get out of hand(idiom) – become unmanageable or out of control.नियंत्रण से बाहर होना
